A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GenderAlign study. Their main texts, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset assessments, human and LLM evaluations, BBQ and WinoGender results, and data-source ablations.

after.justification: v2 reports original evaluations on the retained tasks and adds an experiment controlling dataset size and bias-category distribution.

M1.justification: The documented generation and alignment procedures remain unchanged: GPT-3.5 generates chosen responses, Alpaca-tuned Llama2-7B generates rejected responses, and alignment uses DPO with QLoRA. The generation prompts are identical in v1 Table 7 and v2 Table 8.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seed datasets and five books, GenderAlign and HH-Harmless alignment data, and dialogue, BBQ, and WinoGender evaluations. The new GD/HD subsets resample existing coverage without introducing another domain or task.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain unaligned and HH-Harmless-aligned Llama2-7B/13B models, and the Books/CW comparison is retained. The new GD/HD experiment varies sampling and category composition within the existing dataset-based approaches.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 replaces least-biased-response selection rates with rankings scored 3, 2, and 1. New Section 5.3 introduces four 1,000-sample conditions controlling dataset source and category distribution. Section 4 also changes the stated HH-Harmless classification procedure from GPT-3.5 to human evaluation; this documents a protocol revision without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Section 5.3 and Table 5 test whether alignment differences arise from dataset quality or category distribution through matched-size GD/HD subsets. The source ablation remains, now in Section 5.4. The dedicated three-example Llama2-13B refusal case study in v1 Table 9 is removed, while the shared comparative example remains.

E5.justification: Both versions aggregate human judgments and report Fleiss' kappa. Updated kappa values and another application of the same agreement statistic change results, rather than statistical reporting practice. Neither introduces repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Main and source-ablation selection percentages are replaced by ranking scores, preventing direct performance comparisons across those metrics. BBQ Table 3 changes throughout: 7B-GenderAlign accuracy changes from 28.6% to 30.7% and SDIS from 3.9 to 0.4. New Table 5 adds distribution-control results; agreement coefficients also change. WinoGender Table 4 and Figure 2 values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: No theoretical result, proof, or formal derivation is added or revised. The taxonomy and existing benchmark mathematics are retained, with benchmark explanations moved to Appendix I. The ranking-point change concerns empirical evaluation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and central conclusion retain the same claims: an approximately 8,000-dialogue alignment dataset, four bias categories, and better gender-bias mitigation than HH-RLHF. The additional analysis supports these retained contributions.

C2.justification: v2 newly attributes the advantage to both dataset quality and category distribution, while removing the explanation that 13B-Harmless performs poorly because of refusals or uninformative answers. Limitations now emphasizes human annotation bias and drops the explicit GPT-3.5-generated-data caveat, despite retaining GPT-based generation. These changes substantially revise the explanatory account.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses the 9:1 split, two RTX 3090 GPUs, AdamW, evaluator recruitment and screening, compensation, and detailed annotation guidelines. These are disclosures, not demonstrated changes to existing settings. Conversely, some validation/classification sample counts disappear, and the GenderAlign download link is replaced by a statement promising release under Apache-2.0.

R1.justification: v2 adds Qi et al. and Baumgartner et al. to motivate concerns about contaminated alignment data, plus a wage reference. It expands discussion of the already-cited CORGI-PM corpus. The overall positioning relative to existing bias datasets remains stable.

P1.justification: Book descriptions and benchmark explanations move into appendices, alignment-related discussion moves into the introduction, and results prose is revised. Appendix organization expands and several references and labels are corrected. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds two annotation-guideline figures and the distribution-control table, removes the dedicated refusal-example table, and adds shaded model rows and fuller benchmark captions. Existing appendix tables are largely relocated or renumbered. The workflow and category-distribution graphics are identical, and the overall layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: The matched-size distribution controls and detailed evaluator guidance improve the evidence and its auditability relative to v1. The gain is limited by unresolved reporting problems: the four-model study lacks an explicit fourth-place scoring rule, and the BBQ discussion incorrectly claims higher 13B-GenderAlign accuracy than Harmless despite Table 3 showing 39.2% versus 40.4%. Removal of the dataset access link and GPT-generation limitation also weakens transparency.
